subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw retire the shipped `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` value now and use this doctor migration, including disabling enabled legacy configurations only when their active OTLP signals cannot export?
rationale: The code can enforce either policy, but choosing whether a previously accepted persisted value should become invalid and how much legacy telemetry state to preserve is a maintainer-owned compatibility decision.

options.title: Accept the value-aware doctor migration
options.body: Reject `grpc` going forward and retain this migration, which preserves usable stdout-only logs but disables legacy enabled configurations whose OTLP signals could never export.

options.title: Keep the existing config value temporarily
options.body: Defer schema narrowing until maintainers choose a longer deprecation window or implement real gRPC export support.

options.title: Choose a different migration policy
options.body: Specify an alternative explicit upgrade behavior, then update the migration, docs, and focused tests to match it.

recommendation.title: Accept the value-aware doctor migration
recommendation.body: Reject `grpc` going forward and retain this migration, which preserves usable stdout-only logs but disables legacy enabled configurations whose OTLP signals could never export.
